newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BASKET DEALS DOMINATE BCE CURRENCY FUTURES MARKET.
newsitem.headline: BASKET DEALS DOMINATE BCE CURRENCY FUTURES MARKET.

text.p: December basket deals dominated currency futures trade on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Monday, traders said.
"Most currency movements are rather unpredictable at the moment, thus basket deals, although offering a lower yield, provide more security," said Janois Szolyka of Swap brokerage.
In basket deals mark and dollar futures are sold or bought in proportion to their relative weight in the National Bank of Hungary (NBH)'s basket against which the forint is floated.
The NBH basket is made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar.

Accordingly, half of Monday's turnover in volume terms was for December German marks which rose 5 fillers to 117.21 and about another quarter was for December dollars which dropped 69 fillers to 194.71.

December Ecus were the only other maturity that featured heavily in today's trade but Szolyka said that judging from the price, which was about a forint off market prices, it probably was an agency cross.
"Since the Ecu is no longer in the basket, it became fairly illiquid and such deals hardly make any difference to the market," he said.
4,700 lots for December Ecu, 4,000 for December mark and 2,000 for December dollar changed hands on Monday, accounting for the bulk of the day's modest 12,908 lots or 2.25 billion forints turnover.
The Budapest Stock Exchange, which trades mark, dollar and Ecu futures, saw no currency futures deals.
